name: Justice
symbolism: A figure in a red robe sits on a throne between two pillars, behind which hangs a purple veil. In one hand the figure holds a raised double-edged sword, in the other a pair of scales in balance. A white shoe shows beneath the robe, and the gaze is calm and direct.
upright: Justice invites you to take an honest look at the situation, taking all its sides into account. The card speaks of the link between choices and their consequences. This may be a good moment to name the facts and decide in line with your own sense of fairness. Clarity often brings relief, even when it calls for honesty with yourself.
reversed: Reversed Justice may suggest difficulty accepting responsibility, or a feeling that something remains out of balance. It is worth checking whether your judgement of the situation is too harsh, towards others or towards yourself.
reflection: What would this situation look like if you looked at it from every side?
What do you want to take responsibility for, and what is not yours to carry?
advice: Act fairly and weigh up all sides. A decision based on facts and truth will bring a fair result.
adviceReversed: Something is out of balance. Check whether you are being completely honest with yourself and with others before you pass judgement.

name: The Hanged Man
symbolism: A man hangs head down, tied by one foot to a T-shaped wooden beam from which leaves are sprouting. His other leg is bent to form a cross, and his hands are hidden behind his back. A halo shines around his head, and his face stays calm.
upright: The Hanged Man describes a time of suspension that can bring an entirely new view. When action brings no results, it often helps to stop and look at things from a different side. The card encourages you to let go of the need for immediate solutions. Understanding often ripens in apparent stillness.
reversed: The reversed Hanged Man may point to impatience with the pause, or to staying suspended longer than necessary. It can also be an invitation to notice what you can now let go of in order to move on.
reflection: What will you see if you look at this matter from the completely opposite side?
What can you give up to make room for something new?
advice: Do not hurry. Stop and look at the matter from a different side: letting go may give you more than fighting.
adviceReversed: Waiting is no longer useful. If you are stuck in suspension, it is time to make a decision and move on.

name: Death
symbolism: A figure in black armour rides a white horse, carrying a black banner with a white rose. Before it stand and kneel people of different stations, from a ruler to a child, each reacting differently to its arrival. In the background, between two towers, the sun is rising.
upright: In tarot, Death symbolises the closing of one chapter and the passage to the next, not a physical end. The card speaks of a transformation that frees up space, just as autumn prepares the ground for spring. It may encourage you to say goodbye to habits, roles or beliefs that have served their purpose. The rising sun in the background is a reminder that after an ending comes a new beginning.
reversed: Reversed Death may point to resistance to a change that is ripening from within anyway. Sometimes it is an invitation to let something go gently instead of keeping it alive by force.
reflection: Which stage of your life is naturally coming to an end?
What could appear if you made room after what is leaving?
advice: Close what has ended. Let the old stage go: only then will there be room for the new.
adviceReversed: You are holding on to something that has already passed. The change will come anyway, and it will be easier if you stop resisting it.

name: Temperance
symbolism: A winged angel in a white robe pours water between two cups, standing with one foot on the bank and the other in a stream. On the angel's chest is a triangle inscribed in a square. Yellow irises grow nearby, and a path leads towards mountains, above which an arc of light shines.
upright: Temperance speaks of the art of combining opposites and looking for the golden mean. The card encourages calm, gradual action instead of extreme solutions. It may concern balancing work and rest, or reason and emotion. Harmony is not a fixed state but a continuous, attentive tuning.
reversed: Reversed, the card may point to a lack of balance: excess in one area at the cost of another. It is a signal to look at where a gentle correction of proportions is needed.
reflection: Which two areas of your life need better balancing right now?
What could change if you acted in small, patient steps?
advice: Look for the golden mean. Combine opposites and act calmly, step by step: moderation is your strength right now.
adviceReversed: You are overdoing something, whether work, emotions or expectations. Restore the balance before you start anything new.

name: The Devil
symbolism: A horned figure with bat wings sits on a dark pedestal, raising one hand and holding a lowered torch in the other. Two naked figures with small horns and tails are chained to the pedestal. The chains around their necks are loose: they could take them off.
upright: The Devil invites you to look at what keeps you stuck: habits, beliefs or dependencies. The card is not a verdict but an opportunity to become aware of mechanisms working outside your attention. The loose chains are a reminder that many limits can be loosened once they are named. It is also a space for an honest meeting with your own shadow.
reversed: The reversed Devil may mean the beginning of freeing yourself from a pattern, or the moment when an attachment becomes clearly visible. It can be an invitation to win back your freedom gently but steadily.
reflection: Which habit or belief limits you more than you want to admit?
What would change if that chain turned out to be looser than it seems?
advice: See what is holding you: a habit, a fear, a dependency. Name it honestly; the chain is looser than it seems.
adviceReversed: You have a chance to break free. Take the first step away from the pattern that harms you: it is easier now than before.

name: The Tower
symbolism: A tall tower on a rocky peak is struck by lightning, which knocks off its crown. Flames burst from the windows, and two figures fall against a dark sky. Small sparks in the shape of the Hebrew letter yod float all around.
upright: The Tower describes the moment when something that seemed stable suddenly demands reassessment. Such a change can come as a surprise, but it often reveals a truth that had been hidden. The card encourages you to check which structures were built on shaky foundations. Once things are cleared up, there is room for something more authentic.
reversed: The reversed Tower may point to putting off a necessary change, or to a transformation happening more on the inside than on the outside. Sometimes it is a signal that something can be rebuilt gradually before the tension builds up.
reflection: Which belief or arrangement needs an honest check today?
What could be built in place of what is no longer working?
advice: Do not prop up what is crumbling. Accept the change and build something on stronger foundations.
adviceReversed: You are avoiding an inevitable change. It is better to face it now, on your own terms, than to wait for the shock.

name: The Star
symbolism: A naked woman kneels at the edge of a pool and pours water from two jugs, one into the water and the other onto the land. Above her shines a large eight-pointed star surrounded by seven smaller ones. A bird has alighted on a tree in the background.
upright: The Star brings a sense of respite and quiet hope. The card invites you to rest and to rebuild trust in yourself and the world. It is a good time for dreams that do not have to be realised straight away in order to give you strength. The simplicity of the scene is a reminder that you can show yourself without masks.
reversed: Reversed, the Star may point to tiredness or hope that has dimmed for a while. It is an invitation to look for small sources of light and give yourself time to recover.
reflection: What gives you a sense of hope today, however small?
How can you look after your rest in the coming days?
advice: Have hope and act from it. The worst is over: give yourself time to recover and look to the future with trust.
adviceReversed: Have you lost faith that things can get better? Start with one small step that will give you back a sense of meaning.

name: The Moon
symbolism: A moon with a human face shines over a night landscape, and drops of light fall from it. A dog and a wolf howl at it on either side of a path that winds between two towers towards distant hills. A crayfish crawls out of the water in the foreground.
upright: The Moon describes a state in which not everything is clear and imagination suggests different versions of events. The card encourages you to look with curiosity at dreams, hunches and fears without treating them straight away as facts. It is a time to move carefully, step by step. Uncertainty is often a stage that comes before understanding.
reversed: The reversed Moon may suggest that the fog is beginning to lift, or that fears are gaining disproportionate power. It is worth separating what is known from what the imagination adds.
reflection: What in this situation is a fact, and what is your interpretation?
Which dream or hunch has been coming back to you lately?
advice: Not everything is clear right now, and that is all right. Do not make final decisions in the fog; trust your intuition, but check the facts.
adviceReversed: The fog is beginning to lift. Call your fears by their names: many of them will turn out smaller than they seemed.

name: The Sun
symbolism: A naked child with a garland and a red feather on its head rides joyfully on a white horse, holding a great red banner. Above shines a radiant sun with a face, and sunflowers bloom behind a low wall.
upright: The Sun brings the energy of clarity and simple joy. The card encourages you to enjoy what is good and to share your warmth with others. It may describe a moment when things become clear and action comes easily. It is also an invitation to get in touch with childlike spontaneity.
reversed: Reversed, the Sun's joy may be muted or hard to accept fully. Sometimes it is also a signal not to pretend to be cheerful when a moment of honesty is needed.
reflection: What gives you real, simple joy?
How can you allow yourself more lightness this week?
advice: The answer is yes. Act openly, with joy and confidence: this is a good time to show yourself.
adviceReversed: Joy is close, but something is obscuring it. Let yourself enjoy what you already have instead of waiting for the perfect moment.

name: Judgement
symbolism: An angel emerges from the clouds and blows a trumpet hung with a flag bearing a red cross. Below, from open coffins floating on water, naked figures rise (adults and a child) with their arms stretched upwards. Snowy mountains can be seen in the background.
upright: Judgement describes a moment of awakening in which your own path becomes clearer than before. The card encourages you to take stock of your experiences and draw conclusions from them without harsh judgement. It may be an inner calling to take up something that has long been important. It is also a space for forgiving yourself and others.
reversed: Reversed, the card may point to judging yourself too critically, or to drowning out an inner calling. It is worth asking what is holding you back from answering what calls you.
reflection: What do you feel an inner calling towards?
What can you forgive yourself for so that you can go on with a lighter heart?
advice: You have heard an inner calling: answer it. Take stock of the past, forgive yourself and make the decision.
adviceReversed: You are judging yourself too harshly or putting off an important decision. Stop waiting for a sign: the sign has already come.

name: The World
symbolism: A figure wrapped only in a purple sash dances inside an oval wreath of leaves, holding two wands. The wreath is tied at top and bottom with red ribbons, and the heads of an angel, an eagle, a lion and a bull appear in the corners of the card.
upright: The World describes a sense of wholeness and the completion of an important stage. The card invites you to appreciate the road you have travelled and how different experiences have come together into a coherent whole. It is a good moment for celebration and gratitude. The end of one cycle naturally prepares the ground for the next.
reversed: Reversed, the World may point to unfinished business or difficulty closing a stage. It can be an invitation to notice what is still missing for a sense of completeness.
reflection: What are you already achieving that you do not yet fully appreciate?
What needs closing before you begin the next chapter?
advice: Bring the matter to a close and appreciate what you have achieved. This stage is complete: you can confidently move on to the next.
adviceReversed: The last step towards closure is missing. Finish what you have started before you take on something new.
